I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat here, and I grow wheat here. The land is good, flat, and the county has wells for irrigation. I have 8 mu of contracted land — all of it goes into winter wheat and then summer maize. That is the only rotation that makes sense to me. Wheat keeps us fed and pays decent in June. Maize goes into October and the buyers come to the village. I do not gamble with vegetables or cotton — those need knowledge I do not have and markets I do not trust.

For wheat I will use Shimai 15, the improved variety the seed shop in town sells. Everyone here uses it. I will spread fertilizer before plowing — urea and diammonium phosphate, the same bags I buy every year. I always irrigate four times: before sowing to settle the soil, then in winter to protect the roots from cold, then at jointing, and again at heading. I spray twice — once for weeds early on, once for powdery mildew when the weather gets warm in April. I use a rotary tiller now, renting the machine from the village cooperative. I expect around 450 jin per mu, which is normal for me.

For maize I will plant Xianyu 335 hybrid seed right after the wheat harvest in June. No tilling — I sow straight into the stubble, it saves me effort and the machine does it fine. I water twice unless there is good rain in July. I spray once for borers. Harvest in late September. I expect about 550 jin per mu.

I am 67. My son is in Shijiazhuang. I manage these 8 mu myself with my wife and hire a laborer for harvest. I do what I know.
